To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) SSD failure rates are higher than previously reported in the literature, (ii) SSD failures are correlated with the number of erase cycles and the amount of data written, (iii) SSD failures are more likely to occur when the SSD is full, (iv) SSD failure rates vary by manufacturer, (v) SSD failures occur at different times during the day, and (vi) SSD failures are not correlated with the temperature of the SSD.

flash SSD reliability is a complex function of many variables, that the failure rate is highly non-uniform across the lifetime of the flash SSD, and that the failure rate of flash SSDs is highly dependent upon the workload.

flash-based SSDs are not reliable enough for use in mission-critical systems.
flash memory reliability is not a problem that can be solved by a single component or layer of the system stack; it is instead a problem that requires collaboration between all layers of the stack.
